html:
The Jitajita, also spelt Yitayita, are an Aboriginal Australian people of southern New South Wales, in the dry country between the lower Lachlan and the Murrumbidgee rivers.

Their neighbours were the Nari Nari and Madi Madi, and to the north the Barindji. Their name, like those of several neighbours on the Murray and its rivers, comes from their word for "no". Sheep runs took up the river frontages in the 1840s, pushing people away from the water.
sum: The Jitajita, also spelt Yitayita, are an Aboriginal Australian people of southern New South Wales, in the dry country between the lower Lachlan and the Murrumbidgee rivers.
